title: Custom Normalization from a CSV File
author: Opentrons

steps.title: Prepare CSV input file
steps.instruction: Create a CSV file containing the columns: sample_id, dna_conc_initial (ng/µL), dna_conc_target (ng/µL, allowed range 5–40), and volume_target (µL, allowed range 30–100). Fill each row with the corresponding values for up to 96 samples.

steps.title: Upload CSV and start protocol
steps.instruction: In the Opentrons app, load the custom normalization protocol, upload the prepared CSV file, and start the run. The robot will read the file, calculate for each sample the fold dilution, the volume of sample to transfer, the volume of water to add, and will flag whether an intermediate dilution is required (sample transfer < 2 µL) or the sample must be skipped (sample transfer > 30 µL).

steps.title: Transfer water to output plate
steps.instruction: Using the single‑channel P20 and P300 pipettes, dispense the calculated water volume into each designated output‑plate well. After each dispense, return the tip to the tip rack for reuse.

steps.title: Transfer sample (or intermediate dilution)
steps.instruction: Using the single‑channel P20 and P300 pipettes, dispense the calculated sample volume into each output‑plate well. If the calculated sample volume is less than 2 µL, first prepare a 10X intermediate dilution by mixing 2 µL of the sample with 18 µL of water, mix thoroughly, and then use this dilution as the source for the transfer. After each tip use, rinse the tip once in 10 % diluted bleach before discarding it in the trash bin.

substeps.instruction: If sample_transfer < 2 µL, prepare intermediate dilution: add 2 µL sample + 18 µL water, mix.
Transfer the appropriate volume (sample or intermediate dilution) to the output well.
Rinse the used tip 1× in 10 % diluted bleach, then discard.

steps.title: Download output CSV file
steps.instruction: When the run finishes, open the Opentrons app, go to the Devices tab, select your robot, click the three‑dot menu in the upper right → Robot Settings → Advanced → Launch Jupyter Notebook. In the opened browser window locate the generated output CSV file and download it to your computer.
